label: NOTE: what this set covers, and what it cannot
why: All three of V90SdDetector.cpp's functions: the constructor, the destructor and reset().  Two things here cannot be mutated into a caught failure and are deliberately absent.  The first is the STORE ORDER of the four arguments, which no observer can distinguish.  The second is the spelling of the float copies: the object copies bits and our build converts through x87 (finding F1242), so a mutation that made the copy a conversion would already agree with our build and a mutation that made it a bit copy would agree with the blob -- neither is a difference this binary can see, and the sweep leaves signalling NaNs out for that reason.  The argument-to-offset mapping IS covered, and it is covered by absolute offset on the blob's object as well as ours, which is what makes the two out-of-order stores (+0x10 and +0x04) non-vacuous.  `process(float)` is covered too, and the entries for it are worth a word: its three comparisons resolve the UNORDERED case in two different directions (finding F1401), so the middle one is spelt as a negation and the mutation that spells it the natural way is the entry that proves the negation is not decoration.  A QUIET NaN is therefore very much in this half of the sweep -- it arrives from the object's own 0/0 rather than from an argument -- and it is the signalling one, and only the signalling one, that stays out.

label: the constructor does not clear the counter
the destructor frees nothing
the destructor frees without testing the pointer
the destructor nulls what it freed
why: NO TEST CAN CATCH THIS ONE, and not because the test is weak: the store is not in the binary.  A store to a member in a DESTRUCTOR is dead by definition -- the object's lifetime is ending -- and `-flifetime-dse`, on by default at -O2, deletes it.  Measured, not argued: compiling this file with and without the store under the tree's exact flags gives BYTE-IDENTICAL text for the whole object, and adding `-fno-lifetime-dse` makes `movl $0x0,0x14(%ebx)` appear in `~V90SdDetector` in the second one and not the first.  The blob does not null either, so the reconstruction is right whichever way the compiler went; what this entry records is that the claim in the source comment is unfalsifiable under this build and must not be asserted in the test as though it were checked.
